accounts.browser_login_msg:
Log in with your {what} {who} account in the browser window that opened.
This closes by itself when you're done.
accounts.channel_moderator: Someone else's: you're a {role} there, so you read and moderate it
accounts.channel_theirs: Someone else's: you read and moderate it with your account
accounts.channel_tooltip: Click to search for a channel. Empty: your own.
accounts.channel_viewer: Someone else's: you're only a viewer there, so you can read and chat but not moderate. Ask the channel to make you a moderator
accounts.connect_on_start_tooltip: On by default: it connects by itself once you are logged in and a channel is set.
accounts.guide:
Account is who you log in as. It doesn't have to own the channel: to moderate someone else's chat, type their channel. On Twitch, what needs the owner's login (channel points, bits, polls) is left out.
Changing the channel starts a clean chat and community for it; the old ones come back if you type it again.
accounts.integrations.intro: Services your actions can control. Each one stays off, with nothing running, until you set it up.
accounts.kick.help: Sending on Kick needs your own Kick app: kick.com > Settings > Developer > Create app, redirect URL {url}, every scope ticked. Paste its client ID and secret here.
accounts.locked_default: Saved logins are locked: the system keyring is locked or wasn't ready
accounts.login_broadcaster_first: log in or pick a channel
accounts.spotify.about: Song requests from chat and playback control from actions (Spotify Premium). Configure connects your own Spotify app.
accounts.spotify.help: Spotify Premium is required. Create an app in the Spotify developer dashboard, add http://127.0.0.1:45564/callback as a redirect URI, select Web API, and paste the client ID below. Add your Spotify account under User Management if needed.
accounts.spotify.name: Spotify
accounts.spotify.need_client_id: Paste the client ID of your Spotify app first.
accounts.standby_default: Standby, connects when the stream starts

accounts.tiktok_sending.title: TikTok account
accounts.tiktok_sending.help:
TikTok uses the account in your own browser for search, authenticated reading and sending. Streamerz works in the background, without a helper tab or window.

1. Open chrome://extensions (edge://extensions on Edge), turn on Developer mode, and choose Load unpacked. Select this folder:
accounts.tiktok_sending.after:
2. Click Log in below if you need to sign in to TikTok. After that, you can close the browser window if background apps stay enabled.

TikTok may restrict automated use. Use a separate account if needed.
accounts.tiktok_sending.remove_confirm: Stop sending to TikTok? The extension is refused from now on and its folder is deleted. Remove it from the browser too.
accounts.twitch.sub_counter_help: The sub counter counts every sub, resub and gifted sub (Get/Set Twitch Sub Counter Count). Every time it reaches the rollover it starts again and Sub Counter Rollover fires.

accounts.youtube.help: Sending on YouTube needs your own Google client: console.cloud.google.com > new project > enable YouTube Data API v3 > OAuth consent screen (External, Publish) > Credentials > OAuth client, Desktop app. Leave Video ID empty to follow the channel's current live.

input.no_terminal: No password dialog (polkit) or terminal was found, so nothing was changed. The commands to run as administrator are in the log.
input.not_done: The access wasn't changed. The terminal window showed what happened.

input.removed: Access removed. Devices already open stay readable until the next restart.
input.terminal_done: Done. You can close this window.
input.terminal_why: Streamerz needs your password to change its udev rule. This is all it runs:
input.windows_mouse: Works in every program, except ones run as administrator.

settings.about.tagline: A light stream automation app, made in Rust.
settings.autostart.about_linux: Run Streamerz when you log in.
settings.memory.saver.about: Applies after restart. Designed for background use.
settings.memory.effects: No chat history, Community tracking, credits, avatars or emote catalogs.
settings.memory.first_words: First Words stays enabled using temporary disk storage.
settings.memory.files: Existing Community files stay untouched. Commands and connections stay enabled.
settings.chat.youtube_tag.about: Display @handle instead of plain channel names in YouTube chat.
settings.chat.fade_in.about: How long a new line takes to appear. 0 shows it at once.
settings.chat.fade_out.about: How long a line takes to go when its time is up. 0 takes it away at once.
settings.chat.keep_history.about: Keep recent messages in memory so you can read and send chat. Turning this off reduces memory use; commands and triggers still run.
settings.chat.keep_history.memory_saver: Memory Saver keeps chat history off until you restart with it disabled.
settings.chat.lifetime.about: A line goes from the chat, and from memory, this long after it was said. 0 keeps them.
settings.chat.per_platform.about: The most lines each platform's chat keeps in memory (10 to 1000). The oldest go first.
settings.chat.total.about: The most lines all the chats keep together (10 to 1000). The oldest go first.
settings.dates.about: How lists, history and the chat show a day.
settings.debug_log.about: Also log details for tracking down a problem.
settings.instance_name.about: What tools connected to the WebSocket server see this as.
settings.language.about: The language of the app: the system's by default, English when the system's isn't here. Applies the next time Streamerz starts.
settings.start_hidden.about: Open in the tray; click its icon for this window.
settings.theme.about: Follow the system (dark or light, and its accent colour), or pick one.
settings.times.about: 12 or 24 hours, for chat lines and history.
